title: Arts Fund paused; taxi fares and accessibility funding increased
subtitle: Also: road tender, cultural grants, non-profit child care, covered bridge, tent city reporting, measles update.
overview: Regional Council temporarily paused funding and administrative support to the Region of Waterloo Arts Fund, citing bullying and harassment of Regional staff and governance concerns, until a third-party expert review is done {{vote:m12}}. To keep supporting artists this year, the Region will work with the Waterloo Region Community Foundation to administer 2024 arts grant applications {{vote:m13}}.

Council also raised the taxi meter drop rate from $3.50 to $4.50 and increased accessible taxi funding programs {{vote:m11}}. It approved 2024 Key Cultural Institutions grants, with extra costs coming from the Tax Stabilization Reserve {{vote:m7}}, and awarded the tender for the River Road/Bleams Road extension {{vote:m6}}.

Other decisions include exploring non-profit child care space on Regional land {{vote:m8}}, a rehabilitation design for the West Montrose Covered Bridge {{vote:m10}}, and an extension of the Every Child Matters bus mural to September 29, 2024 {{vote:m14}}. Council directed staff to collect outcome data from A Better Tent City, matching other outreach providers {{vote:m17}}. The Medical Officer of Health also gave a respiratory season and measles update.

decisions.item: Region of Waterloo Arts Fund pause
decisions.detail: Council temporarily paused funding and administrative support to the Arts Fund, citing bullying and harassment of Regional staff and governance concerns, pending a third-party expert review.

The Region will enter a temporary agreement with the Waterloo Region Community Foundation to collect, review and administer 2024 arts grant applications, with the Region funding the recommended recipients.

decisions.item: Taxi fares and accessible taxi funds
decisions.detail: Council raised the meter drop rate from $3.50 to $4.50 and approved a new five-year accessibility funding program, increasing Taxi Scrip, vehicle conversion and fare subsidy support.

decisions.item: Key Cultural Institutions grants and capacity fund
decisions.detail: Council approved $840,603 in 2024 grants to four cultural institutions, funded the extra $493,450 from the Tax Stabilization Reserve, and approved terms for the Community Capacity Building Fund.
Council accepted J-AAR Excavating Limited's tender of $11,771,530.55 plus taxes for the Regional Road 56 extension.
Staff were directed to explore community-based non-profit child care spaces on Regional and surplus lands and to consult partners on under-utilized buildings.
Staff were directed to collect outcomes, data and metrics from A Better Tent City that align with existing homelessness outreach agreements.
Council approved the rehabilitation design concept and directed staff to file the Notice of Completion and work with Woolwich on heritage by-law amendments.

debate: A delegate for A Better Tent City said the organization accepts data reporting but serves a hard-to-house population unlike other shelters, and receives a small fraction of the funding of a comparable community.

Supporters of the reporting motion said groups that receive taxpayer money, including those that come directly to council, should meet the same accountability standards, such as financial statements, insurance and referral numbers.

One councillor asked to see what staff would require of A Better Tent City, noting audited statements could be costly. Staff said they would follow the existing framework, and several councillors suggested a later discussion on grant criteria and why the group did not fit the existing structure.

On taxi funding, a councillor asked where the increased accessibility money would come from. Staff said the transportation accessibility reserve, which was projected to stay sustainable for at least ten years.

During the public health update, a councillor's question on language barriers for vaccination notices drew objections from another councillor, who said the framing was inappropriate. Staff said notices include multilingual information sheets.
